_doc: Open-sea legs whose midpoint lies in a box need the listed tech nodes (or a `route:<id>` result an action returns, see sim/engine/action_results.py) held by a party to the trade (not necessarily by every carrier). Coast legs are restricted only by a lane that names edge_classes.

entries.source: South of Cape Bojador the trade winds and current make the return voyage north the problem; Mediterranean and European shipping did not go down the West African coast until the voyages the tree names exp_coastal_africa.
entries.why: Keeps ships without that knowledge from following the African coast south.

entries.source: Rounding the Cape of Good Hope needs the knowledge the tree names exp_africa_circumnavigation.
entries.why: Without it a coast chain joins the Atlantic to the Indian Ocean round Africa.

entries.source: Open-water crossings of the Atlantic south of the North Atlantic island chain (Faroes, Iceland, Greenland) need the knowledge the tree names exp_atlantic_crossing.
entries.why: Open-sea legs across the Atlantic would otherwise need only a square sail.

entries.source: Open-water Pacific crossings need the knowledge the tree names exp_openocean_navigation.
entries.why: Open-sea legs across the Pacific would otherwise need only a square sail.

entries.source: As open_pacific_east, the part of the ocean west of the date line.
entries.why: A box cannot cross the date line, so the Pacific is two boxes.

entries.source: North of the Arctic circle sea ice closes the coast most of the year; an iron hull stands in for ice-capable shipping until a sea-ice layer exists.
entries.why: Without it the graph would send wooden sailing ships along the Arctic coast of Russia.

entries.source: the monsoon passages from Arabia to India and India to Southeast Asia; research notes section 6 on seasonal monsoon sailing.
entries.why: Blue-water crossings of the Indian Ocean need the seasonal wind pattern.
